name: Grand Cabin Hotel Naha Oroku
detail: It's like a hybrid between a capsule hotel and a business hotel. The bed was in a spacious room, so I was able to sleep well. There were plenty of amenities and rentals like hair irons, making it comfortable to stay. The free drink service and meals were convenient; even at late hours, I could purchase frozen food and cup noodles, and with a microwave available, I didn’t have any meal issues. It's just one station from the airport, making it perfect for late arrivals and early departures. However, for those who want to sleep in the next morning, it's hard to say. Everyone starts getting ready before 5 AM for early morning flights, so the sounds of footsteps, doors, and preparations can be bothersome and wake you up. Earplugs are a must!! That way, you might be able to sleep better. Overall, for the price, it was a hotel with good facilities that I would like to use again.

name: Hotel Abest Naha Kokusai Street
detail: The room had a double bed, but there was enough space for two people to spread out their suits. The staff's response was polite and left a lasting impression. Their warm touches included early check-in and a souvenir of sata andagi during checkout. I don't think there were body towels among the amenities.

name: The Kitchen Hostel Ao
detail: I used the service for the first time, and the staff's explanations were thorough, making my stay comfortable. There were plenty of restrooms and showers, so I didn't have to wait to use them, which was great. The shared space was very comfortable, and there was a convenience store nearby, so I had no issues. Despite being reasonably priced, the amenities were well-stocked, leading to a high level of satisfaction.
area: Naha,Okinawa Main island - View on map

name: APA HOTEL NAHAMATSUYAMA
detail: It is a reasonable walking distance from Kencho-mae Station, and there are several convenience stores nearby. The hotel has excellent access, connecting directly to Kokusai Street. Whether you find Matsuyama's entertainment district appealing depends on your purpose. During the off-season, the prices are even more affordable, and it offers great value with a large public bath. The breakfast is delicious, so please be sure to include the breakfast option when you stay.
area: Naha,Okinawa Main island - View on map

name: Daiwa Roynet Hotel Naha Kokusai-dori
detail: It is close to Makishi Station and has covered walkways, so even during sudden rain showers, you can move around without getting wet. Kokusaidori and Sakurazaka are also nearby! The room was clean, and the breakfast was delicious. One downside was that I could occasionally hear voices in the hallway or the cleaning sounds from the neighboring room.
area: Naha,Okinawa Main island - View on map

name: Y's Cabin & Hotel Naha
detail: If you only need a place to sleep, it's a clean and very cost-effective accommodation. You can't store things like suitcases, but the front desk lends out chains. The large public bath was spacious and clean. I didn't particularly mind the noise from those around me. On the first floor, there's a simple drink bar and a place to eat food you bring in. It's located just one block back from Kokusai Street, making it quiet.
area: Naha,Okinawa Main island - View on map

name: Green Rich Hotel & Capsule Naha Artificial hot spring Futamata Yunohana
detail: I came to Naha for my child's hospital visit! Since it was summer vacation, I thought it would be nice to go to the pool and art museum with my child, so I chose this hotel for its convenience. There are quite a few shops around that might be a bit too stimulating for kids, but there is a convenience store nearby, and the monorail station is a 10-minute walk away. The staff at the hotel breakfast and the front desk during my late night inquiries were very nice. The bathroom was clean and comfortable, and I even managed to take a morning bath! The bed was very spacious, even for me and my 7-year-old child! The room was small, but it had an air purifier, a kettle, and a bathtub. I had a comfortable stay! Thank you very much!

name: THE NEST NAHA
detail: <Advantages> 1. The breakfast is delicious. Both my parents, child, and my husband and I enjoyed the breakfast. The restaurant is clean, and although there aren’t many food options, we were able to eat well and feel full every morning. 2. We chose a place with a pool because it was difficult to go out often with a child and parents, but both the child and parents had a great time at the pool. 3. It's a new building, so everything is clean overall. The bathroom is spacious. We had a room with a bathtub, and the bathroom is large and the bathtub is deep. The shower was a little inconvenient, but overall, I was satisfied with it. 4. There’s an event offering complimentary drinks like beer, wine, juice, and cola from 6 PM to 7 PM. We don’t drink alcohol, so we went up just to have a juice and then came back down, but it seems like it would be great for those who enjoy beer. By the way, snacks are not provided, and outside food is not allowed. 5. The subway station is close. On our return day, we considered taking a taxi to the airport, but since we hadn’t ridden the Yui Rail before, we decided to walk with our luggage, and the station was relatively close, and the airport is not far either. It seems like it took less than 30 minutes to get to the airport. <Disadvantages> 1. Like most hotels in Japan, there is not enough space to place luggage. We had one large suitcase and one small one as we were staying with our child, and there wasn’t much room to spread them out. However, I think this might be the case in any hotel. 2. It may not be a significant downside, but they do not serve lunch or dinner apart from breakfast. Our family was looking for meals so we wouldn’t have to go out, but aside from breakfast, there were no meals available. It seems there aren't many guests, which might be why. 3. It would have been nicer if the floors were wooden, but that cannot be helped, and it would be good if more attention was paid to cleaning the head of the bed during cleaning. There was quite a bit of dust accumulated there. <Notes> We stayed for two nights, and no cleaning was provided. If you put used towels outside your door, they will leave new towels at your door. If you put the trash bin outside, it will be emptied. Honestly, we didn’t need cleaning during our two-night stay, and it was convenient that only the towels and trash needed to be taken care of. We used the washing machine, which cost 600 yen for two hours of washing and drying. For those who might use it, keep that in mind. Overall, it was a satisfying hotel, and if we visit Okinawa again, I think we would return.

name: Prince Smart Inn Naha
detail: It's somewhat far to the international street, but it's not to the extent that you can't walk there. Overall, the cleanliness of the accommodation is good, and while the parking fee is expensive, it's not unreasonable when calculated on a daily basis. The soundproofing is excellent and I am satisfied with the value for money. It was a twin room, but since the room was small, we pushed the beds together and it was actually quite nice.

name: HOTEL THE CUBE Naha Kokusai Street
detail: I stayed here for 3 nights during my trip to Okinawa. It is located on Naha Street, and there are souvenir shops below, so you don't have to carry heavy bags around. You can also leave your luggage at the counter before check-in, and all the staff members are very kind. :) I usually prefer to use shared facilities to save on accommodation costs, so I didn't experience any inconvenience. Apart from the air conditioning not being adjustable, I had a comfortable stay :)
